correctness.rationale: The three allowed initial states A,B,D and forbidden cyclic DBD follow from the totality constraint. The forced-root process reduces exactly to alternating A–D paths with an A endpoint, excluding full alternating cycles. A fifteen-state transfer realizes precisely these words and has four spurious closed walks on each even all-alternating cycle. The exact characteristic identity of its explicitly defined matrix yields the rational trace generating function; componentwise counts prove a sharp lower bound n attained by the all-B word. Independently simulated 87,360 subsets (n=3..8), checked structural and transfer coefficients through n=11, and reconstructed the characteristic polynomial symbolically with exact Newton identities. No finite test alone is interpreted as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Actual primary full-text comparisons locate the 2017 total-forcing definition and 2018 total-forcing tree theorems, a 2023 scalar sunlet k-forcing computation, and a 2018 ordinary zero-forcing polynomial, none of which states or implies the all-cardinality total-forcing polynomial for sunlets. A relevant later 2025 unicyclic paper was compared at abstract scope; its complete text was not obtained. Searches of the mathematical research record and prior same-series claims found no equivalent. Unindexed implicit prior work cannot be excluded, so novelty is evidence-supported rather than certified.

value.rationale: Sunlets are a standard infinite unicyclic family used in forcing-number research. The result recovers the known type of minimum invariant but additionally determines the complete natural size-distribution of isolate-free zero-forcing sets, a count not recoverable from prior scalar minima. The cyclic alternating-path obstruction explains a nontrivial parity-dependent correction, and the rational multivariate generating function yields uniform explicit coefficient access and a bounded-order recurrence for every n. This is a motivated complete structural enumeration rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
